title: GPart: A GNN-Enabled Multilevel Graph Partitioner
problem: Large-scale graph partitioning requires balancing cut minimization and memory efficiency; existing multilevel methods like METIS use heuristic coarsening and refinement, missing learning-based optimization.
motivation: Graph partitioning is fundamental for distributed graph processing and communication minimization in irregular workloads, but conventional methods lack adaptive optimization.
method: A scalable multilevel framework integrating GNN embeddings with traditional coarsening and refinement techniques. GNN embeddings capture graph structure for improved partitioning decisions during multilevel optimization. Efficient hierarchical coarsening reduces problem size while GNN guidance refines partition quality.
key_novelty: First multilevel graph partitioner integrating GNN embeddings for adaptive partitioning decisions while maintaining memory efficiency through optimized hidden layer sizes.
contributions: 34.13%-42.92% cut size reduction over METIS on Titan23
9.30% improvement over G-kway on DIMACS benchmarks
24.6× and 12.4× normalized memory improvement over GAP and GenPart respectively

metrics.other: Cut size 34.13%-42.92% reduction, 24.6× memory efficiency vs. GAP

primary_theme: GNN-enabled scalable multilevel graph partitioning with memory efficiency
